51.0.0.en: God declares that He will raise up a violent wind against Babylon, which stands against God and against His people. This wind is the kingdom of Media and Persia, and it will destroy her. Here God appears as the Almighty, who uses the power of the earth to carry out His will. He uses Babylon to discipline His people and the nations, then uses Media and Persia to discipline Babylon, so that perhaps all may repent.

51.1.0.en: He likens Media and Persia not only to a destructive wind but to winnowers, that is, those who separate the grain from the chaff by means of a tool called the winnowing fan. Since Babylon has no goodness in her, which is symbolized by the grain, the winnowers scatter the chaff and it flies far away, and Babylon becomes empty, because the grain falls close by while the chaff flies far off. That is, Media and Persia will ruin Babylon and she will become desolate. He also makes clear that Media and Persia will besiege Babylon from every side, killing those in her, while only a few will escape from her.

51.2.1.en: Utterly destroy: kill. God calls Media and Persia to kill the soldiers of Babylon, whether those who shoot arrows with the bow or those who put on armor to protect themselves and attack with swords and spears, so that Media and Persia kill the mighty men, the heroes of Babylon.

51.3.0.en: And so Babylon is filled with the corpses of the slain in all the streets.

51.4.0.en: Here God makes clear that although the Jews in the kingdoms of Judah and Israel sinned by worshiping idols or lusts and angered their God, yet He loves them, since they believe in His name above all peoples. So He disciplines them through Babylon, then punishes Babylon, which was cruel to them, and requires of her all the blood of His people.

51.5.0.en: God calls His people and all the nations who accept His prophecies through the mouth of Jeremiah to flee from Babylon because she will be destroyed. Everyone who believed the word of God and fled was saved from death.

51.6.0.en: God likens Babylon to a golden cup because of her great wealth, but she is in the hand of the Lord her Creator, who uses her to discipline His people and the nations, and when she does not repent, He disciplines her. The sin of Babylon was that she did not only do evil but made the nations stumble by her sins, and He likens this to a cup full of wine given to all the nations to drink, which seduces them and makes them fall into evil. Indeed, through the nations' immersion in evil, she lost her kingdom and became like a madwoman.

51.7.0.en: Balm: a medicine taken from a plant that grew in the south of Palestine.

51.7.1.en: God calls the angels to bring medicine for Babylon, that perhaps she may be healed, but she rejected the word of God through the mouth of the prophets, so she found no medicine that could benefit her. But the people of God accepted the medicine, that is, they repented, and so He brought them back safely to their land at the beginning of the rule of Media and Persia. Thus Babylon was shattered, while the people of God returned to worship Him in Jerusalem.

51.8.0.en: The people of God realized Babylon's insistence on evil and her refusal to repent, so they left her, saved themselves, and returned to Jerusalem.

51.9.0.en: Zion: Jerusalem. The people of God rejoiced that He had brought them back from captivity and forgiven their sins, so they returned to Jerusalem proclaiming how God had rescued them when they repented and brought them back to worship Him in His temple.

51.10.0.en: God calls the soldiers of Media and Persia to prepare themselves to fight Babylon and take vengeance on her, carrying out the will of God because of her injustice toward His people.

51.11.0.en: He continues speaking to the soldiers of Media and Persia, telling them to besiege her, to set watchmen around her, and to prepare an ambush to break into the city from under its walls, through the bed of the river Euphrates, which they had dried up.

51.12.0.en: He rebukes Babylon, who relied on her wealth, on her abundance of water through the great river Euphrates that passes through her, and on the great quantity of silver and gold in her treasuries. He warns her that she will be seized by the hand of Media and Persia, and God will measure out destruction upon her. Thus He likens the destruction to a measure filled with evil and plunder which He pours out upon her.

51.13.2.en: God concludes His words about the punishment of Babylon by saying that the armies will rush upon her in great numbers like locusts and with a great noise, and will ruin her.

51.13.3.en: Do not rely on your strength or your wealth, for all this passes away, and do not make light of evil, for God watches over everything. Return to Him with repentance, rely on Him, and trust in His love, that He will receive you however great your sins.

51.13.5.en: 15- He hath made the earth by his power, he hath established the world by his wisdom, and hath stretched out the heaven by his understanding. 16- When he uttereth his voice, there is a multitude of waters in the heavens; and he causeth the vapours to ascend from the ends of the earth: he maketh lightnings with rain, and bringeth forth the wind out of his treasures. 17- Every man is brutish by his knowledge: every founder is confounded by the graven image: for his molten image is falsehood, and there is no breath in them. 18- They are vanity, the work of errors: in the time of their visitation they shall perish. 19- The portion of Jacob is not like them: for he is the former of all things, and the rod of his inheritance, the LORD of hosts is his name. 20- Thou art my battle axe and weapons of war: for with thee will I break in pieces the nations, and with thee will I destroy kingdoms; 21- And with thee will I break in pieces the horse and his rider; and with thee will I break in pieces the chariot and his rider;

51.13.6.en: 22- With thee also will I break in pieces man and woman; and with thee will I break in pieces old and young; and with thee will I break in pieces the young man and the maid;

51.13.7.en: 23- I will also break in pieces with thee the shepherd and his flock; and with thee will I break in pieces the husbandman and his yoke of oxen; and with thee will I break in pieces captains and rulers.

51.13.8.en: 24- And I will render unto Babylon and to all the inhabitants of Chaldea all their evil that they have done in Zion in your sight, saith the LORD. 25- Behold, I am against thee, O destroying mountain, saith the LORD, which destroyest all the earth: and I will stretch out mine hand upon thee, and roll thee down from the rocks, and will make thee a burnt mountain. 26- And they shall not take of thee a stone for a corner, nor a stone for foundations; but thou shalt be desolate for ever, saith the LORD.

51.14.0.en: Jeremiah praises God, the Creator of the whole universe, and what he mentions here in (vv. 15-19) is a repetition of what he said before in (ch. 10:12-16). For He is the Creator of heaven and earth and the whole world.

51.15.0.en: God is also the mover of everything in the universe: He moves the winds so that the rain falls, and gives a command to the lightnings, so they come forth with their flashing and the rain falls with them. He likens the power of God the Almighty to treasuries in which He keeps the winds, and commands them, and they come out of them.

51.15.1.en: Vv. 17, 18: Brutish: he has become ignorant and foolish.

51.15.2.en: Before the greatness and knowledge of God, man's ignorance is revealed, for his knowledge is very limited before the unlimited wisdom of God. Man's ignorance is shown in his portraying gods in the form of idols that have no power in them, and so he points here to the weakness of Babylon, which trusted in idols, before the unlimited power of God. All the images that the craftsmen cast are vanity, and their weakness is shown in that they do not help their owners in times of distress, such as the attack of Media and Persia on Babylon and their destruction of her.

51.16.0.en: These are the idols of Babylon, which have no power. But as for the people of God, Israel, their King, who is indicated by the rod that the king holds in his hand, is very strong; He overcomes all the power of the world and delivers His people who rely on Him, who are His inheritance, that is, His kingdom and those who follow Him. He is also their inheritance, since they inherit in Him the Kingdom of Heaven.

51.17.0.en: After the praise offered to God ends, He addresses a great nation, which He likens to a battle axe that in war breaks in pieces everyone it meets. It is either:

51.17.1.en: 1- The nation of Media and Persia, which shattered Babylon and took possession of all the nations of the world.

51.17.2.en: 2- Or Babylon, which shattered the nations of the world, and then God punishes her in (v. 24).

51.18.0.en: This axe shatters all the military powers of the nations of the world, represented by horses and war chariots.

51.19.0.en: With this axe He kills all people, men and women, old and young, and all the youths.

51.20.0.en: He also kills and ruins the various kinds of trades, whether the shepherds and their flocks or the farmers and their crops. He even kills the rulers of these nations.

51.21.0.en: God decides that He will punish Babylon for all her evils and her injustice toward His people in Jerusalem.

51.22.0.en: He likens great Babylon to a mountain that exalts itself in its pride, so God burns it and rolls it down like a small stone, that is, Babylon becomes utterly weak. Just as she destroyed the rest of the earth, Babylon is now destroyed because of her evil.

51.23.0.en: The stones of this mountain become useless and are not fit as stones for any new building, whether strong stones to be placed in the corner of a wall or even ordinary stones for any building. That is, Babylon becomes ruined and abandoned, and not fit for any person to live in.

51.23.1.en: Contemplate the greatness of God in creation so that you praise Him, glorify Him, rely on Him, and rejoice in His presence with you. Then you will no longer be troubled by the movements of others and their threats, but will live in peace in the bosom of your God.

51.23.3.en: 27- Set ye up a standard in the land, blow the trumpet among the nations, prepare the nations against her, call together against her the kingdoms of Ararat, Minni, and Ashchenaz; appoint a captain against her; cause the horses to come up as the rough caterpillers. 28- Prepare against her the nations with the kings of the Medes, the captains thereof, and all the rulers thereof, and all the land of his dominion. 29- And the land shall tremble and sorrow: for every purpose of the LORD shall be performed against Babylon, to make the land of Babylon a desolation without an inhabitant. 30- The mighty men of Babylon have forborne to fight, they have remained in their holds: their might hath failed; they became as women: they have burned her dwellingplaces; her bars are broken.

51.23.4.en: 31- One post shall run to meet another, and one messenger to meet another, to shew the king of Babylon that his city is taken at one end,

51.23.5.en: 32- And that the passages are stopped, and the reeds they have burned with fire, and the men of war are affrighted. 33- For thus saith the LORD of hosts, the God of Israel; The daughter of Babylon is like a threshingfloor, it is time to thresh her: yet a little while, and the time of her harvest shall come.

51.24.0.en: Ararat: a region in Armenia, north of Lake Van.

51.24.1.en: Minni: a region next to Ararat in Armenia.

51.24.2.en: Ashchenaz: a people descended from Gomer, the grandson of Japheth (Gen 10:3), who dwell in Armenia.

51.24.3.en: God speaks to Media and Persia so that they call the surrounding peoples, whom Media had previously subjected to her authority, to go out with her to fight Babylon. The Median commander raises the banner of war and the peoples follow him to attack Babylon. The meaning is that huge numbers of soldiers fought Babylon and ruined her.

51.25.0.en: Prepare: set apart. In sum, all the peoples subject to the authority of Media will attack Babylon, since Media had become the strongest nation in the world at that time, Persia had united with her, and many peoples had submitted to her, by whom she crushed the kingdoms of the earth, the first of which was Babylon.

51.26.0.en: He portrays the greatness of the Median attack on Babylon, in that the earth shakes and trembles under the feet of the soldiers gathered around Babylon to destroy her, because God the Almighty wished to punish Babylon.

51.27.0.en: Failed: that is, dried up, and the meaning is that their courage grew very weak, that is, they became without strength.

51.27.1.en: Her bars: the timbers that support the pillars of the house and cover it as a roof.

51.27.2.en: The mighty men of Babylon, that is, the commanders of her armies, were afraid and were unable to fight, and fled, taking refuge in their strongholds, and their courage was lost, so they became as weak as women when they saw their houses and palaces burned with fire.

51.28.0.en: When any war takes place, soldiers who are able to run swiftly hurry to tell the king the outcome of the war. Here the post, that is, the swift runner, gives the news to another runner, so the news reaches the king quickly that Babylon has fallen from one end of the city to the other, that is, all of it has fallen.

51.29.0.en: And they told the king that the roads leading to the city had been taken over by the enemies, and that when the Babylonian soldiers took refuge among the stalks of the reeds to hide among them, the enemies burned the reeds to put an end to them all, and the whole Babylonian army was in weakness and confusion.

51.30.0.en: He likens Babylon to a threshingfloor, which is a broad place where grain is threshed by means of threshing sledges drawn by animals. That is, the feet of the enemies trample Babylon to kill those in her and cut off their heads from their bodies with swords, as the grain is separated from the chaff by the threshing sledge. Thus the heads of all her inhabitants will be reaped and the city will be utterly destroyed. And just as Babylon ruined the kingdom of Judah, Egypt, and Moab, so she too will be ruined (ch. 4:7).

51.30.1.en: Do not anger God by your deeds, lest He allow everyone to rise against you to trouble you; and if you sin, return to Him quickly with repentance, for He is merciful and long-suffering. [4] The destruction of Babylon because she wronged the people of ... (vv. 34-40)

51.30.2.en: 34- Nebuchadrezzar the king of Babylon hath devoured me, he hath crushed me, he hath made me an empty vessel, he hath swallowed me up like a dragon, he hath filled his belly with my delicates, he hath cast me out. 35- The violence done to me and to my flesh be upon Babylon, shall the inhabitant of Zion say; and my blood upon the inhabitants of Chaldea, shall Jerusalem say. 36- Therefore thus saith the LORD; Behold, I will plead thy cause, and take vengeance for thee; and I will dry up her sea, and make her springs dry. 37- And Babylon shall become heaps, a dwellingplace for dragons, an astonishment, and an hissing, without an inhabitant. 38- They shall roar together like lions: they shall yell as lions' whelps. 39- In their heat I will make their feasts, and I will make them drunken, that they may rejoice, and sleep a perpetual sleep, and not wake, saith the LORD. 40- I will bring them down like lambs to the slaughter, like rams with he goats.

51.31.0.en: Judah cries out like a weak woman before the cruelty of the Babylonians, saying that Nebuchadnezzar the king of Babylon has devoured her goods and destroyed her, and swallowed all her glory like a dragon that swallows and devours anything before it, and drank all her goods so that she became an empty vessel, and cast out all her inhabitants who fled from the swords of his soldiers.

51.32.0.en: The kingdom of Judah groans, declaring that she has been wronged and that Babylon will be called to account for the blood of Judah that was shed in the streets.

51.33.0.en: God comes forth to defend His people, and becomes an adversary to Babylon in place of His weak people. So He withholds her goods from Babylon by drying up the river Euphrates, on which the goods of Babylon depended, when Media diverted the river Euphrates and dried it up.

51.33.1.en: 37: When God ruins Babylon, she becomes heaps of stones and is abandoned, not dwelt in by man but by beasts such as jackals, and everyone who passes by her is astonished, wondering how the greatest city of the world was ruined, and he knows that the reason is her evil.

51.34.0.en: Lions' whelps: cubs or young lions.

51.34.1.en: The soldiers of Media attack Babylon, and are like young lions that devour everyone they meet, consume all the goods of Babylon, and roar against her with a terrifying roar.

51.34.2.en: In their heat: in their excitement over the pleasures of eating and drinking in celebration of their god.

51.35.0.en: The Babylonians were celebrating the feast of their god Bel and drinking wine with their king, and while they were in the pleasure of their lusts, the Medes attacked them, so they drank the wrath of God and died, to end in eternal torment because of their evils.

51.36.0.en: With he goats: the plural of equipment, which means weapons of war and all of a person's possessions.

51.36.1.en: The Babylonians become like lambs and rams before the power of the Medes, who slaughter them and take their possessions and goods.

51.36.2.en: Be just in your dealings with those around you, even if they have no power. Do not wrong anyone, and give everyone his due, not only in money but in speech, in expressing himself, and in his comfort. And do not rejoice that by your selfishness you have obtained what you want at the expense of others, for you will be called to account for all of this.

51.36.3.en: [5] The ruin of Babylon and the deliverance of the people of ... (vv. 41-53:)

51.36.4.en: 41- How is Sheshach taken! and how is the praise of the whole earth surprised! how is Babylon become an astonishment among the nations!

51.36.5.en: 42- The sea is come up upon Babylon: she is covered with the multitude of the waves thereof. 43- Her cities are a desolation, a dry land, and a wilderness, a land wherein no man dwelleth, neither doth any son of man pass thereby. 44- And I will punish Bel in Babylon, and I will bring forth out of his mouth that which he hath swallowed up: and the nations shall not flow together any more unto him: yea, the wall of Babylon shall fall. 45- My people, go ye out of the midst of her, and deliver ye every man his soul from the fierce anger of the LORD. 46- And lest your heart faint, and ye fear for the rumour that shall be heard in the land; a rumour shall both come one year, and after that in another year shall come a rumour, and violence in the land, ruler against ruler. 47- Therefore, behold, the days come, that I will do judgment upon the graven images of Babylon: and her whole land shall be confounded, and all her slain shall fall in the midst of her. 48- Then the heaven and the earth, and all that is therein, shall sing for Babylon: for the spoilers shall come unto her from the north, saith the LORD. 49- As Babylon hath caused the slain of Israel to fall, so at Babylon shall fall the slain of all the earth.

51.36.6.en: 50- Ye that have escaped the sword, go away, stand not still: remember the LORD afar off, and let Jerusalem come into your mind.

51.36.7.en: 51- We are confounded, because we have heard reproach: shame hath covered our faces: for strangers are come into the sanctuaries of the LORD'S house.

51.36.8.en: 52- Wherefore, behold, the days come, saith the LORD, that I will do judgment upon her graven images: and through all her land the wounded shall groan. 53- Though Babylon should mount up to heaven, and though she should fortify the height of her strength, yet from me shall spoilers come unto her, saith the LORD.

51.37.0.en: Sheshach: the one sunk in water, and the meaning is Babylon, which is on the river Euphrates, that is, with abundant water around her.

51.37.1.en: God shows the reversal of fortunes in great Babylon, who used to boast over all the countries of the world, and how she collapsed and was ruined because of her pride and her evils.

51.38.0.en: He likens the attack of Media and Persia to the raging sea that covers Babylon and drowns her, that is, destroys her, since the soldiers of Media and those who follow her were very many, as if they were the sea.

51.39.0.en: After the ruin of Babylon, she will be abandoned, and no man will live in her.

51.40.0.en: The symbol of Babylon's power was her god Bel. Babylon used to wrong and devour all the peoples, and she is symbolized by the god Bel who devoured all the peoples, but he is nothing before the power of God; he is merely an image to which they offer animals for him to eat, though in truth it is his priests who eat them (Dan 13). That is, God proclaims the weakness of Babylon and of her god, who is shattered, and likewise her great walls, in which she boasts over all the peoples, are broken and torn down.

51.41.0.en: He calls His people dwelling in Babylon to flee from her when Media and Persia attack her, and not to trust in her strength, in which she prides herself, because she will be ruined, so the people of God flee from her quickly. All these prophecies God proclaimed about 70 years before the ruin of Babylon, and no one believed them except His people, who fled and so saved themselves by their obedience to God.

51.42.0.en: Ruler against ruler: Media and Persia rule over Babylon. God reassures His people when they see the attack of Media and Persia on Babylon, and declares to them that the reports of Media and Persia's domination of the world will follow one another, so they should not be troubled by the fall of Babylon and the domination of Media and Persia, because God will bring them back to their land at the beginning of the rule of Media and Persia.

51.43.0.en: By the attack of Media and Persia, they shatter Babylon and her gods, that is, her idols, to proclaim that their gods are stronger than the gods of Babylon, and they kill the men of Babylon, and everyone of them who remains alive is put to shame.

51.44.0.en: Because God is the one who commanded the ruin of Babylon, the heavens and the earth rejoice in this. The earth symbolizes the cities of the world that Babylon wronged, so they gloat over her at her ruin, while the heavens symbolize the angels who rejoice at the removal of evil and its punishment. The attack of Media and Persia on Babylon will come from the north.

51.45.0.en: Here God shows that the punishment of Babylon is because of her injustice toward the people of God, and just as she killed the men of the people of God, Media and Persia kill the men of Babylon.

51.46.0.en: He speaks to the people of God who are fleeing from Babylon, that they should hasten their flight and think of returning to Jerusalem to renew her temple and offer worship to God.

51.47.0.en: God reminds His people of the shame they felt when Babylon attacked Jerusalem, entered the temple of God, and ruined it.

51.48.0.en: Because Babylon defiled the temple of God, God shatters her idols by the hand of Media and Persia, and kills and wounds her inhabitants.

51.49.0.en: God decides in the end that however much Babylon exalts herself and relies on her strength and greatness, God will punish her and destroy her.

51.49.1.en: Flee from evil and from keeping company with the wicked, and from their places that make you stumble, and from everything that makes you fall into sin, for this flight of yours means your faith in God and purity, and God will help you, bless you, and keep every evil far from you. [6] The shattering of great Babylon (vv. 54-58:)

51.49.2.en: 54- A sound of a cry cometh from Babylon, and great destruction from the land of the Chaldeans: 55- Because the LORD hath spoiled Babylon, and destroyed out of her the great voice; when her waves do roar like great waters, a noise of their voice is uttered: 56- Because the spoiler is come upon her, even upon Babylon, and her mighty men are taken, every one of their bows is broken: for the LORD God of recompences shall surely requite.

51.49.3.en: 57- And I will make drunk her princes, and her wise men, her captains, and her rulers, and her mighty men: and they shall sleep a perpetual sleep, and not wake, saith the King, whose name is the LORD of hosts. 58- Thus saith the LORD of hosts; The broad walls of Babylon shall be utterly broken, and her high gates shall be burned with fire; and the people shall labour in vain, and the folk in the fire, and they shall be weary.

51.50.0.en: God describes what will happen in Babylon when Media and Persia attack her: the sound of the shattering of her houses and walls will rise, accompanied by the cry of her inhabitants, who fall by the sword and are ruined, and the voices of pride coming from the king and the princes will come to an end and be replaced by the sound of fear and shame and the cry of those who flee.

51.51.0.en: God punishes Babylon for her evils, so He shatters her by means of Media and Persia, kills her heroic soldiers, and shatters her weapons of war.

51.52.0.en: All the princes and great men of Babylon fall like those who have drunk a great deal of wine, so they reel and fall to the ground, and will not rise, because they have died.

51.53.0.en: Weary: very tired. This shows the weakness of men however great their strength: Babylon spent great effort and vast sums in building her walls, but they will be shattered, so that all the peoples may know that protection comes from God and not from material strength.

51.53.1.en: Do not waste all your time in the works of the world and forget your goal, who is God. And if anxiety fights you, turn to Him, and not to gathering money and mustering the forces of the world, for they will neither protect you nor give you peace.

51.53.2.en: [4] The reading of the prophecies in Babylon (vv. 59-64:)

51.53.3.en: 59- The word which Jeremiah the prophet commanded Seraiah the son of Neriah, the son of Maaseiah, when he went with Zedekiah the king of Judah into Babylon in the fourth year of his reign. And this Seraiah was a quiet prince. 60- So Jeremiah wrote in a book all the evil that should come upon Babylon, even all these words that are written against Babylon. 61- And Jeremiah said to Seraiah, When thou comest to Babylon, and shalt see, and shalt read all these words; 62- Then shalt thou say, O LORD, thou hast spoken against this place, to cut it off, that none shall remain in it, neither man nor beast, but that it shall be desolate for ever. 63- And it shall be, when thou hast made an end of reading this book, that thou shalt bind a stone to it, and cast it into the midst of Euphrates: 64- And thou shalt say, Thus shall Babylon sink, and shall not rise from the evil that I will bring upon her: and they shall be weary. Thus far are the words of Jeremiah.

51.54.0.en: Jeremiah chose a believing man from among the followers of King Zedekiah, Seraiah the son of Neriah, the prince of the camp, that is, the chief of the city in which the people settle and dwell. It seems that he was a ruler over Jerusalem, and he was a devout man and the brother of Baruch the son of Neriah, the prophet, the scribe of Jeremiah's prophecies and his disciple. Seraiah was going with King Zedekiah in the fourth year of his reign to Babylon to renew his covenants and his allegiance to Babylon, although after his return he broke his covenant and began to incline toward the king of Egypt.

51.55.0.en: Jeremiah wrote his prophecies that he had proclaimed about Babylon, which are written in chs. 50, 51. He wrote them himself in a book, that is, a large piece of leather or papyrus. Because of the gravity of these prophecies, Jeremiah wrote them himself and did not have Baruch write them, so as not to expose him to danger from Babylon's anger against him and the occupation of his land, and he bore the responsibility, risking his life in carrying out the commands of God. Here Jeremiah's fatherhood and his self-giving as a servant appear.

51.56.0.en: Jeremiah asked Seraiah, when he entered Babylon, to gather the Jews who had been taken captive to Babylon and read to them the words of this book, and to affirm that Babylon will be ruined.

51.56.1.en: This speech may seem very strange to unbelievers: how did Jeremiah call his people to submit to Babylon and now declare that she will be ruined? The reason, of course, is that they should accept God's discipline by submitting to Babylon until they repent, and then not cling to the goods of Babylon nor seek shelter in her, because she will be ruined on account of her evil, and they must believe in God and take refuge in Him.

51.57.0.en: Jeremiah commanded that the ruin of Babylon be confirmed by an illustrative example: that he should bind the book in which the prophecies are written to a stone and then throw it before the eyes of the people into the river Euphrates, declaring that Babylon will sink in this way, that is, be ruined.

51.57.1.en: God alerts you to the events of the world so that you repent and return to Him. So He shows you the fall of the powers of the world and the punishment of the wicked, so that you do not rely on the wicked world. Contemplate the works of God before you so that you may believe in Him and live with Him.

51.57.2.en: A summary of the events of the fall of Jerusalem and the captivity. Jeremiah mentioned the fall of Jerusalem in chs. 39, 40, and this event is also mentioned in (2 Kgs 24, 25) and (2 Chr 36:17-21). He closed the end of ch. 51 by saying that these words are the end of the prophecies of Jeremiah, from which it is understood that ch. 52 was added to the book, and most likely the one who wrote it was Ezra the priest. It summarizes the events of the fall of Jerusalem, the plundering of the spoils of the temple, and the captivity of the Jews, then the beginning of God's mercies, which will be completed by the return from captivity.
